feed.title: NPR Topics: Climate
feed.subtitle: NPR's full coverage of climate change and related issues.

entry.title: A new report finds many Chinese provinces are reducing their use of coal
entry.summary: China is the world's largest emitter of planet-warming pollution. But a new report this week finds the country is transitioning away from fossil fuels including coal.

entry.title: 'Her body temperature was 106': How heat is killing Americans in their homes
entry.summary: Heat kills thousands of people across the U.S. every year. The risk is especially high for the millions of Americans who live in manufactured housing like mobile homes and trailers.

entry.title: Forecasters sound the alarm over a powerful El Nino climate pattern
entry.summary: Forecasters expect the El Niño weather pattern to strengthen significantly this year, raising the risks of extreme weather around the world well into 2027.

entry.title: Inside the failed mission to eliminate FEMA
entry.summary: David Richardson worked to eliminate the country's top disaster agency when he led FEMA last year. Now, he says the administration has abandoned that goal.

entry.title: U.N. climate report warns world will soon cross a dangerous threshold
entry.summary: A new United Nations report finds that the world will soon pass a dangerous threshold for climate warming. Countries had agreed to limit warming to that level to avoid the most extreme impacts.

entry.title: Chevron's expansion in Venezuela has implications for the oil industry and the planet
entry.summary: Chevron is expanding its current operations in Venezuela. The deal expands the company's footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty in Venezuela.

entry.title: Chevron to expand in Venezuela, days after the U.S. and Venezuela strike oil deal
entry.summary: Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.

entry.title: He died of 'natural causes.' But his mother says she knows what killed him: heat
entry.summary: When Arizona counts heat-related deaths, Adam Willson isn't included. His story shows how thousands of heat deaths can go uncounted every year in the United States.

entry.title: The U.S.-Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know
entry.summary: The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.

entry.title: NPR spent 2 years tracking deaths from heat. We found a staggering hidden toll
entry.summary: An NPR investigation found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat much more often than official counts show. We explore the reasons why — and how lives can be saved.
